title: Thank people and carry yourself
header_line: My analysis of one book on authority and personal brand. Not a summary of the book. Not affiliated with or endorsed by the author or publisher.

lines.text: Who do you thank on the way in?
A student who worked at a door said: it is not about the money, it is the frequency; you build relationships with the people who work the rope. I always thank them and ask how they are doing.
I said: that is a very wise thing we just learned, thanking people.
A student who works in hotels said that important guests are well groomed, articulate, kind and appreciative of the staff, and often come back with gifts or meals for them.
I said that is beautiful wisdom, that they come in with gifts for everybody.
I said that I learned from a mentor to walk into a bank with a box of pastries and hand it out, and that I know my regular coffee shop and printer by name and order for their staff how they like it.
A student described a hard-nosed client who opened up when they went deeper into the relationship and found out a personal need.
I said that gave a window with him: it was not transactional, he realized you are long-term relationship people who listen and care, and that is what referrals are all about.

exercise.title: Five minutes
steps: Write who you pass every week and have not thanked.
Write a small gift you could bring.
Write the people whose names you know.
Write a relationship that is only transactional.
Write what you could ask about their life.

check.q: What did a student say it is about, not the money?
What did I say I learned from a mentor?
choices: To bring pastries to the bank

check.q: What did I say referrals are about?

recap: Thank people. Bring something small. Build the relationship.
